unit.can_do_en: return something and explain what is wrong.

brief.situation_en: Maria at the electronics shop. Emma serves her.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Moi! Mä haluun palauttaa nää kuulokkeet.
lines.text_kirja: Hei! Minä haluan palauttaa nämä kuulokkeet.
lines.gloss_en: Hi! I want to return these headphones.

judge.reason: Only register differences: moi/hei, mä/minä, haluun/haluan, nää/nämä.
Okei/selvä and niis/niissä are register variants; same question.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: The left side doesn't work at all.

judge.reason: Onks sul/onko sinulla is a register difference; same question about a receipt.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: On, täs. Mä ostin ne viime viikolla.
lines.text_kirja: On, tässä. Minä ostin ne viime viikolla.
lines.gloss_en: Yes, here. I bought them last week.

judge.reason: täs/tässä and mä/minä are register variants; same time (last week) and content.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text_kirja: Haluatko sinä uudet vai rahat takaisin?
lines.gloss_en: Do you want new ones or your money back?

judge.reason: Haluuk sä/haluatko sinä and takas/takaisin are register differences; same options.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text_puhe: Okei, hetki. Mä haen ne varastost.
lines.text_kirja: Selvä, hetki. Minä haen ne varastosta.
lines.gloss_en: OK, one moment. I'll get them from the stockroom.

judge.reason: Okei/selvä, mä/minä, varastost/varastosta are register differences; same place (storeroom).

forms.why_en: Moi is the everyday spoken hello. Books and formal texts write hei.
Means 'I'. Spoken Finnish often says 'mä'.
Haluta with -n for 'I': haluan. Speech says haluun.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech shortens nämä to nää. Books write nämä.
Adds -t for more than one: kuuloke becomes kuulokkeet.
Okei is the everyday spoken OK. Books write selvä, which means clear.
'What.' A question word in nominative singular, asking what the price is.
Adds -ssä for 'in': ne becomes niissä, 'in them'. Speech says niis.
Means 'is': present tense, 3rd person singular, going with 'Helsinki'.
vika means fault. Mikä on vikana means 'what is wrong', with -na.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Ei on its own answers 'no'. Speech says it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Means 'is...?'. The question ending -ko turns 'on' (is) into a question.
Sinä with -lla. With on it means 'you have'. Speech shortens it to sul.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Here: in the inessive, literally 'in this'; said when handing something over. Spoken as täs.
ostaa means to buy. -i- marks the past and -n goes with minä: ostin.
Ne means they, for things. Speech also uses it for people.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Adds -lla for time: viikko becomes viikolla, kk turning into k.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 2nd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: In Haluuksä, speech says haluu for haluat and -k for -ko, then joins sä.
Means 'you' (one person). Spoken: 'sä'.
Adds -t for more than one: uusi becomes uudet.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Money you get back is said with -t: raha becomes rahat.
Means 'thanks!', said on its own as a reply.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to fetch, to pick up, to apply
forms.why_en: Hakea changes to hae- and takes -n for 'I': haen.
Adds -sta for 'from': varasto becomes varastosta. Speech drops the last vowel: varastost.
